answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place jobs or receive reputation. A new identity starts with no trusted history, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must fund its own bond, and misconduct can forfeit it. This makes a swarm of fake agents costly to create and keep active, while honest agents recover their stake. A sonnet-writing quill may harbor many names, but every name still needs capital at risk.
